official.deadline_note: BI publishes a single annual deadline of 'March 1' for all master applicants and gives no year on the page. The scholarship page currently states that only candidates admitted to a master's programme commencing Autumn 2026 will be considered, so the 1 March 2026 round has closed; the application portal opens 1 November, making 1 March 2027 the next scholarship deadline for the following autumn intake. Non-EU/EEA citizens who need a residence permit must apply for admission by 15 June, and late scholarship applications are not considered.
official.application_cycle: Annual autumn intake: admission application portal opens 1 November, scholarship and admission deadline 1 March, awards notified by end of April; published page refers to the master's programme commencing Autumn 2026.
official.status_note: The scholarship page states 'The application deadline is March 1' and that only candidates admitted to a master's programme commencing Autumn 2026 will be considered - that round's 1 March 2026 deadline has passed. The same annual 1 March deadline governs the next intake, with applications opening 1 November.
official.tuition_coverage_note: International Applicants: 'Scholarships will cover full tuition fees for up to two years and a stipend for living expenses of NOK 50,000 per semester, if the student achieves the academic progression requirements.' Norwegian and International Applicants who are residents of Norway, and Sivok applicants: 'Scholarships will cover full tuition fees for each semester, for up to two years, if the student achieves the academic progression requirements.'
benefits: International Applicants: full tuition fees for up to two years and a stipend for living expenses of NOK 50,000 per semester, if the student achieves the academic progression requirements.
Norwegian and International Applicants who are residents of Norway: full tuition fees for each semester, for up to two years, if the student achieves the academic progression requirements.
Sivok Applicants (3rd year): full tuition fees for each semester, for up to two years, if the student achieves the academic progression requirements.
International applicants who apply for the BI Presidential Scholarship are also considered for the Master's International Scholarship; no separate scholarship letter is required.
Recipients act as BI Ambassadors - spokespeople, assisting in recruitment efforts and promoting a good study environment.
You may apply for more than one scholarship; BI awards only one scholarship per applicant, tied to a specific programme and campus and non-transferable.
eligibility: Candidates must have a minimum overall GPA of 'A' on the ECTS scale or the equivalent top-level grade on international grade scales to be considered.
Students in the 3rd year of the Sivøk programme are eligible to apply.

Candidates with Norwegian or international citizenship. Candidates with international citizenship who have completed a bachelor's degree in Norway are considered residents of Norway for this scholarship.
Candidates admitted to the first year of a master's degree programme at campus Oslo or campus Bergen, except for the BI-Luiss Joint Masters in Marketing.
Only candidates seeking their first master's degree are considered for master's scholarships.
International candidates eligible for tuition fee reduction and/or a student loan in Norway from Lånekassen are considered as domestic applicants for scholarship purposes.
requirements: Always apply for a scholarship at the same time as you apply for admission on the online application portal; applications for scholarship are not accepted by email except for 3rd year Sivøk applicants.

Upload a CV/resume and a scholarship application letter outlining why you should be considered, maximum one page, combined into one PDF file, in the section marked 'Scholarship' in your online application for admission.

Include all required documentation for admission to a master's programme; the scholarship application is considered only if a complete application for admission has been submitted and the offer of admission is accepted.
Only the scholarship application and documentation submitted at the time of the admission application are considered; no additional documentation is accepted once submitted.
For scholarship consideration, the GMAT/GRE and an English aptitude test must be taken before 1 March; conditional offers are not granted without them.
Academic progression requirements: full study progression (30 ECTS) in each semester and a minimum cumulative GPA of a 'B' on the BI ECTS scale after each academic semester.
documents: CV/resume combined with a one-page scholarship application letter in a single PDF, uploaded to the 'Scholarship' section of the admission application.

Official university/college transcripts and diplomas with an official explanation of the grade scale used, in a Scandinavian language or English (or a certified translation accompanied by the original).
GMAT (Focus 555 / 10th edition 600) or GRE (158 Quantitative) score report, mandatory for bachelor's degrees from outside Norway and the Nordics.
TOEFL/IELTS/PTE/Cambridge English test score, or an approved waiver.
One-page CV with relevant education, work experience, volunteering and leadership experience.
Passport copy of the identification page and a financial declaration on BI's template (international applicants).
selection_criteria: Scholarships are awarded based on excellent academic grades, not on financial need.
All candidates are assessed according to the ECTS scale; applicants with international bachelor's degrees have their grades converted to the ECTS scale.
Only applicants who have been admitted to a master's programme and have applied as instructed are considered, and only if the offer of admission has been accepted.
BI ensures the distribution of scholarships across master's programmes.

BI reserves the right to award scholarships according to institutional priorities, which may include prioritising specific master's programmes, diversity and gender distribution, or selected partner schools of BI.
Other factors that may influence awarding could be other academic achievements, GMAT/GRE/CAT scores, extracurricular achievements, and special personal achievements.
coverage: Full tuition fees for up to two years (tuition is invoiced per semester; the award is renewed each semester subject to the academic progression requirements).
Living expenses of NOK 50,000 per semester for international applicants.
Travel, installation, course literature, excursions, re-sit examinations and student welfare organisation membership are not covered by the award.
application_method: Open the application from the chosen master's programme page on bi.no and log in to the online application portal (apply.bi.no); the portal opens 1 November.
Select the scholarship section and upload the combined PDF containing the CV/resume and the one-page scholarship application letter.
Submit the complete admission application with all required documents before the 1 March deadline; scholarship applications are not accepted by email.
Accept the offer of admission while awaiting the scholarship decision, since the scholarship application is only considered if the admission offer is accepted.
3rd year Sivøk applicants apply by emailing their CV and scholarship application letter to info@bi.no with the subject line: BI Presidential Scholarship Application.
official.application_route: Apply for admission and the scholarship together in BI's online application portal before 1 March (3rd-year Sivøk students email info@bi.no instead).
official.citizenship_residency: Candidates with Norwegian or international citizenship; candidates with international citizenship who have completed a bachelor's degree in Norway are considered residents of Norway for this scholarship, and international candidates eligible for Lånekassen support in Norway are treated as domestic applicants.
official.international_eligibility: International applicants are eligible: those who are not residents of Norway receive full tuition plus a NOK 50,000 per semester living-expenses stipend, while international citizens who completed a bachelor's degree in Norway (or qualify for Lånekassen) are treated as domestic applicants and receive tuition coverage only. Non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens pay a 30% tuition fee differential unless they hold an exemption.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Admission to the first year of a master's degree programme at campus Oslo or campus Bergen, except the BI-Luiss Joint Masters in Marketing; admission requires a completed 180 ECTS bachelor's degree in business administration, finance or economics, or 180 ECTS with at least 80 ECTS in a field relevant to the specialisation.
official.duration: Up to two years (two academic years) of a master's programme, maintained by full study progression of 30 ECTS per semester
official.description: BI Norwegian Business School awards this entrance scholarship to applicants with superior academic records admitted to a master's degree programme at campus Oslo or campus Bergen. International applicants receive full tuition fees for up to two years plus a stipend for living expenses of NOK 50,000 per semester, while Norwegian applicants and international residents of Norway receive full tuition fees only. Scholarships are awarded on academic merit rather than financial need, and every recipient must meet the published academic progression requirements and act as a BI Ambassador.
official.program_type: Entrance scholarship for Master of Science (first year of a master's degree programme)
official.english_requirement: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, TOEFL iBT 90, Pearson PTE Academic 62, Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE) 176 or C2 Proficiency (CPE) 180; exemptions for two or more years of higher education taught in English, EU/EEA/Council of Europe school-leavers with at least 7 years of English as first foreign language, and IB Diploma holders. An English aptitude test must be taken before 1 March to be considered for a scholarship.

verification.notes: Award wording, eligibility, application route, March 1 deadline, notification timing and progression requirements were read directly from BI's own BI Presidential Scholarship, scholarships hub, admissions and tuition fee pages on bi.no; no aggregator sources were used. The living-expense figure (NOK 151,690 per year for 2026-27) comes from BI's own tuition fee page, which also confirms standard master tuition of NOK 128,200 per academic year.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a merit-only entrance scholarship for the strongest master applicants at BI's Oslo or Bergen campuses, worth full tuition for two years plus NOK 50,000 per semester if you are an international (non-resident) student. Everything hinges on one date: the scholarship must be requested inside the admission application before 1 March, and BI will not consider anything sent later or by email. Because the award is renewed per semester, you must keep 30 ECTS of progression each semester and a cumulative B average on the BI scale, so it rewards applicants who are confident they can sustain top grades. Domestic and Norway-resident applicants should budget realistically: they receive tuition coverage only, with no living stipend.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-graded master's applicants (an 'A' on the ECTS scale or the top level of their national scale) who have already booked GMAT/GRE and an English test and can meet the 1 March deadline for Oslo or Bergen.
application_readiness_checklist: Book GMAT (Focus 555 or 600 for the 10th edition) or GRE (158 Quantitative) and an English test early enough to sit them before 1 March, and have scores sent to BI (GMAT: search for BI in the institution field; GRE code 0497; TOEFL code 0529).
Check whether you qualify for a GMAT or English-test waiver on BI's exemption page and upload the completed waiver form with your application if so.
Write a one-page letter that argues academic excellence, not financial need, then merge it with your one-page CV into a single PDF under 25 MB.
Confirm your target programme is eligible: any first-year master's at Oslo or Bergen except the BI-Luiss Joint Masters in Marketing, and that you have never completed a master's degree.

Prepare transcripts and diplomas with an official grade-scale explanation, translated and certified where needed, and reflecting 5 semesters (three-year degree) or 7 semesters (four-year degree) if you are still studying.
If you are a 3rd-year Sivøk student, email your CV and letter to info@bi.no with the subject line 'BI Presidential Scholarship Application' instead of using the portal.
Accept your admission offer as soon as it arrives - BI only considers the scholarship once the admission offer is accepted.
common_rejection_risks: No GMAT/GRE or English score in hand before 1 March: BI states these applicants are not considered for a scholarship and are not granted conditional offers.
Adding documents after submission - BI accepts nothing further once the application is in, so a missing grade-scale explanation or waiver form cannot be fixed later.
A GPA below the 'A' ECTS threshold or the equivalent top grade on your national scale; scholarship grading is on academics alone, not need.
Holding a previous master's degree, or applying to the BI-Luiss Joint Masters in Marketing, which is explicitly excluded.
Emailing the scholarship application instead of filing it in the portal (only 3rd-year Sivøk applicants may email).
Not accepting the admission offer while waiting, or missing the acceptance date printed on the scholarship offer, which is withdrawn and given to another candidate.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: International applicants are covered for tuition and receive NOK 50,000 per semester, but BI's own estimate of living expenses for 2026-27 is NOK 151,690 per year, so roughly NOK 50,000 per year of living costs remains unfunded; domestic residents get no stipend at all. Applicants also fund course literature, course excursions, re-sit examinations (NOK 330 per credit in 2026/27) and the semester student welfare organisation membership fee. Non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens face a 30% tuition differential (NOK 128,200 standard master tuition rises to NOK 166,700, or NOK 135,600 to NOK 176,300 for Business Analytics and Data Science for Business) and must show a deposit covering tuition plus one year of living expenses for the residence permit.
document_audit: Electronic diplomas are not accepted - BI returns the application, so upload a scan or photo of the original paper document.
Every transcript must carry an official explanation of your institution's grading scale; without it BI cannot convert you onto the ECTS scale used for scholarship grading.
Certified translations must be submitted together with the original-language document, not on their own.
The name on your documents must match your passport exactly, otherwise BI requires a Norwegian Tax Administration name-change form.
Uploads must be under 25 MB and in PDF, JPG, JPEG or PNG format - combine everything into one PDF rather than sending several large files.
English and GMAT/GRE scores can come either as a direct electronic send from the test provider or a copy of the score report; IELTS copies must show the TRF number.
alerts: The page currently describes the Autumn 2026 intake, whose 1 March 2026 deadline has passed - diarise 1 March for the next round, which opens when the application portal opens on 1 November.
Award offers can arrive at any point in the admission cycle and must be accepted by the date on the offer or they are reallocated; the general notification deadline is the end of April.
You may apply for several scholarships but BI awards only one per applicant, and the award is tied to one programme and campus and cannot be transferred.
To keep the money you must complete 30 ECTS every semester and hold at least a cumulative B on the BI ECTS scale, plus take on BI Ambassador duties.
Scholarship decisions are final and cannot be appealed, so eligibility and deadlines must be right the first time.

Applying for the Presidential Scholarship automatically enters you for the Master's International Scholarship with no extra letter - useful, since BI distributes awards across programmes and institutional priorities.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Open the admission application from your chosen programme page, upload the combined CV-plus-letter PDF in the scholarship tab, submit everything before 1 March, then accept the admission offer and wait for the end-of-April decision.
